requirements.statement: For each informative vector image (<svg>) that has a text alternative, outside the particular cases, the alternative is relevant.

citations.quote: porteuse d’information, ayant une alternative textuelle, cette alternative est-elle pertinente (hors cas particuliers) ?
vérifier que l’alternative textuelle est pertinente

routes.statement: Each source present is relevant: the <title> element, the aria-label attribute and the passage of text linked by aria-labelledby.

citations.quote: S’il est présent, le contenu de l'élément `<title>` est pertinent
S’il est présent, le contenu de l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-label` est pertinent
S’il est présent, le passage de texte associé via l’attribut WAI-ARIA `aria-labelledby` est pertinent
pour les images vectorielles (balise <svg>) l’alternative textuelle pourrait se trouver aussi présente dans une balise <title> ou dans une balise <text>

exceptions.statement: An image used as a CAPTCHA or as an image-test: criterion 1.3 is not applicable to it; criterion 1.4 treats it.

citations.quote: lorsque l’image est utilisée comme CAPTCHA ou comme image-test
le cas des CAPTCHA et des images-test est traité de manière spécifique par le critère 1.4.

exceptions.statement: An image that is the only content of a link: its alternative is the link's text and is evaluated with the links theme.

citations.quote: lorsque l’image est le seul contenu d’un lien, son alternative est l’intitulé du lien. Dans ce cas, l’alternative de l’image devrait être évaluée avec la thématique « Liens ».

exceptions.statement: An image that is the only content of a <button> element: its alternative is the button's label and is evaluated with the forms or scripts theme.

citations.quote: lorsqu’un bouton de formulaire, inséré avec l’élément

rationale.text: Relevance is judgment: code cannot decide whether a text gives the information an image carries. Whether an image carries information, and whether it is a CAPTCHA or an image-test, are judgment too. So no check can fault an alternative as surely irrelevant on an element surely in scope, nor pass a page, and the entry stays at none. The wording lists the sources and asks that each one present be relevant ("S’il est présent"), not only the one the accessible-name order selects; the entry models this as one requirement with one route that names every source. The particular case of criterion 1.3 is an exception: CAPTCHA and image-test images, which criterion 1.4 treats. The two notes of the glossary of an informative image are exceptions too: an image that is the only content of a link has its alternative evaluated with the links theme, and one that is the only content of a <button> with the forms or scripts theme. The first note says "devrait"; listing it can only make the entry claim less. The glossary adds that an svg's alternative may also sit in a <text> element; the wording lists only <title>, aria-label and aria-labelledby, so a <text> element is cited in the route as a place the alternative may be found, and judging it is part of the same judgment. No axe rule is tagged. axe's svg-img-alt is not tagged for this test either: by its own description it ensures that svg elements with an image role have accessible text, which is presence, not relevance. No custom check is registered. Applicability is judgment, because the test applies only to images that carry information and are not CAPTCHA or image-test. Needs is empty: the methodology asks for no assistive technology. The glossary says that where the name computation is only partly supported, the value assistive technologies really render is the alternative; that matters for which text is judged, not for whether the test can be examined, and at none nothing is concluded.

citations.quote: Image qui véhicule une information nécessaire à la compréhension du contenu auquel elle est associée.
Pour une image porteuse d’information, l’alternative textuelle apporte l’information nécessaire à la compréhension du contenu qu’elle véhicule
c’est la valeur réellement restituée par les technologies d’assistance utilisées dans l’environnement de test (ou « base de référence ») qu’il faudra considérer comme alternative textuelle
